argument:
The bull's $7.4bn realised IaaS revenue, up 121%, fairly rebuts a thesis based entirely on unconverted RPO. Actual revenue and EPS improvement are present. Yet the next $664bn of RPO carries a different capacity and funding requirement, and no matched operating-margin or cash bridge establishes returns on that future delivery.

Debt, leases and FCF remain unresolved. The higher policy-rate hurdle is relevant without claiming Oracle-specific repricing, while 13.16x forward vendor P/E does not value the obligations independently. A mixed rebound below SMA-200 on weak volume offers little extra entry support. Prior conversion demonstrates capability, but cannot substitute for evidence that the next infrastructure expansion earns above funding costs.
key_points: Current IaaS growth proves realised conversion.
Future RPO delivery still requires separate funded-return analysis.
Debt, leases and FCF remain unresolved at the quoted valuation.
rebuttal_to_previous: The bull successfully rebuts an entirely-unconverted-business interpretation. It has not answered financing of the next expansion; observed past revenue conversion is not evidence that $664bn RPO becomes adequate cash returns.
